sentences.text: This concept defines the operational scope and principal interfaces for operating and maintaining the offshore wind farm.
The operational boundary covers the wind farm assets, offshore support facilities, control functions, and maintenance activities required to deliver safe electrical generation.
The physical boundary begins at the turbine structures and includes the array of turbines and the Offshore Substation.
The electrical boundary extends through the farm’s export connection to the point where the Grid Interface Relay represents the interface with the external grid.
The concept includes the Turbine Controller, Pitch System, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Rotor Brake Unit, and Turbine Sensor Bus as representative turbine systems.
It also includes the Main Transformer, Export Cable Monitor, SCADA Gateway, and associated monitoring and control functions.
The boundary ends at defined connections to shore-based control, grid operations, ports, suppliers, and emergency services.
Public grid assets beyond the agreed connection point and port operations outside farm-related logistics are outside this concept.
The primary operational objective is to generate electricity reliably while maintaining personnel safety and asset integrity.
Availability objectives are pursued through condition monitoring, timely fault response, planned maintenance, and coordinated access to offshore assets.
Safety objectives require work to be authorized, hazards to be controlled, and personnel and vessels to be accounted for throughout each operation.
Environmental objectives include preventing pollution, minimizing disturbance to the marine environment, and responding promptly to environmental incidents.
The operating model assigns continuous monitoring and dispatch coordination to the Shore Control Room.
The lifecycle assumption is that the concept applies from commissioning and acceptance through routine operation, major refurbishment, and eventual decommissioning.
During commissioning, the system is assumed to transition from construction control to operations control through documented handover and verification.
During normal service, operating decisions are based on validated asset status, approved procedures, current forecasts, and applicable grid instructions.
Planned maintenance is assumed to be scheduled around equipment condition, resource availability, access constraints, and production requirements.
Unplanned maintenance is assumed to use prioritized fault assessment and controlled mobilization appropriate to the severity of the failure.
At end of life, the concept supports safe isolation, removal planning, and transfer of residual operational records to the responsible organization.
The control interface includes operational coordination with the Fleet Dispatch Console and Maintenance Planning Engine.
Marine coordination covers the Crew Transfer Vessel, Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel, Helideck, and applicable vessel operating procedures.
Workforce interfaces include access management through the North Access Scanner, South Access Scanner, and Personnel Tracking Console.
Supply interfaces cover inventory and replenishment coordination through the Warehouse System and Spares Hub.
External interfaces include weather services, metocean observations, grid dispatch, port support, and emergency response organizations.
Cybersecurity, communications, fire protection, and backup power are treated as enabling functions within the farm operations boundary.
